title: Size generation from demand and yield
statement: Before generating, size a unit's item bank from how many certified items each use needs, such as practice, checkpoints, retest forms and review, divided by the expected certification yield.
example: A certification yield of 0.5 means generating twice as many items as must be certified.
detail: A reading course's demand calculator sizes each theme before authoring begins (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/scripts/lane-tools/theme-demand/README.md`). It counts the certified items each consumer needs, practice slots, a 15-item checkpoint, a parallel 15-item form for each funded retest, and shares for spaced review and a cold pool, then divides the total by the certification yield to get the number to generate, along with the authoring load per text. Its default yield of 0.5 rounds a grade 5 campaign that certified 48.7%, and the same file keeps a grade 3 calibration blocking before generation or a grade 3 gate goes live.
against: The yield it divides by is a pricing prior from another grade, not a grade 3 readiness result (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/scripts/lane-tools/theme-demand/README.md`, lines 54-55), so the sizes are estimates until a grade 3 calibration replaces it.

evidence.quote: Sizes a theme BEFORE authoring begins
table of items TO CERTIFY and TO GENERATE, broken down by consumer (practice slots, D15 checkpoints, retest reserve, spaced review, cold pool) plus per-text authoring load.
one 15-item checkpoint per theme and one parallel 15-item form per funded retest cycle
`certification_yield` 0.5 is a historical G5 pricing prior (campaign 48.7%), not a G3 readiness result.
